lastText: STAVKASVODKAHome19141915191619171918HARD MODE — EROSION 2/4-9MANPOWER-5MUNITIONS-7HOME STABILITYIII.1918Signed at Brest-LitovskThe treaty is signed on 3 March 1918, and the date is New Style because the calendar changed in February along with everything else. It gives up Poland, the Baltic provinces, Finland, Ukraine — territory holding a large part of the Empire's population, coal and grain. It is signed because there is no army left with which to decline it. The front that could not be held in 1915 without shells could not be held in 1918 without men, and the men walked home.Settled recordEast Prussia: entered after the concentration was complete. 1915: the Polish salient was held. August 1915: the Grand Duke retained the supreme command. 1916: the South-Western Front attacked alone and spent its best divisions doing it. March 1917: the front commanders advised abdication. June 1917: the offensive was made. Autumn 1914: the northern effort was renewed. The Emperor at headquarters: the question did not arise. October 1917: the headquarters took no side. The officers of this headquarters disperse toward the Don, toward Siberia, and toward the new Republic's own army. What they do next is not this war.Return to file
